observations: The public Angular shell and indexed permit view routes are reachable from a web fetch service.
The Angular bundle certifies POST /api/Searches/Permits/RENumberSearch?searchTerm={RE} followed by GET /api/Permits/{PermitId}.
A bounded detail response includes parcel RE number, lifecycle dates, contractor, invoices, and inspections.
The implementation host times out on the Angular application and receives Akamai Access Denied from the API, so local execution cannot run the contract.
A bounded AWS Batch probe in us-east-1 returned HTTP 200 for metadata, parcel search, and permit detail in 550 ms, 709 ms, and 386 ms respectively.
The AWS parcel search for 044280-0505 returned linked permit identifiers, including a finalized residential roofing permit, without authentication.
The official daily BID ArcGIS All Permits layer returned 3,624,986 records and supports deterministic ordered pagination through the public city map proxy.
The bulk layer exposes parcel RE, full permit number, lifecycle timestamps, status and permit type codes, description, cost, company and contractor identifiers, and last inspection date.
A 100-parcel JaxEPICS soak completed without errors: 93 positive parcels, 7 permitless parcels, 655 references, 50 of 50 detail parcel matches, search p95 885 ms, and detail p95 1,366 ms.
The official public page confirms anonymous historical search by permit, address, parcel RE number, or name.
The reusable Click2Gov session and CSRF form contract was confirmed against the same vendor family.
The implementation host received a CentralSquare support-ID error before a Jacksonville Beach session was issued.
No Jacksonville Beach permit detail was fetched from this egress, so full harvesting is disabled.
BS&A Online terms expressly prohibit scripts, bots, scraping, automated processes, and circumvention of service limits, so no live automated adapter is enabled.
Sanitized parser fixtures preserve the previously observed shape for record RES21-0037, permit key 54715, parcel 171190 0000, details, inspections, fees, and lifecycle dates.
The fixtures cover a terminal zero-result response and pagination without authorizing further automated access.
The predecessor eTRAKiT host returned HTTP 403/503 and is retained as a documented unavailable source.
Complete current BS&A and predecessor eTRAKiT history must be obtained directly from the City of Atlantic Beach.
The official planning page is protected by browser verification and no public historical permit-search endpoint was identified.
The official site publishes permit forms but no public historical permit-search endpoint.
